[{:db/id 17592186092185 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-e321af2f-d67a-5dc4-a077-c6060845ea99"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186092025 :question/problem "Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y-2z=-2 \\ -3y+z=-2 \\ 3x-7y+3z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}.$ Given that $\mathbf x = \langle x,y,z\rangle$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*
![](images/22/220e8838850356768215ed74aefc469edbdc99aa50b9116729329f0e818d6978.svg)" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186092186 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-0807a9e2-ba3b-5d6e-8562-a580bc61f62a"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186092026 :question/problem "Solve the following system of linear equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}3y+x+z=0 \\ z+4y-5=2 \\ 1+2x-y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we organize the system so that the variables are in the correct order and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}x+3y+z=0 \\ 0x+4y+z=7 \\ 2x-y+0z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

![](images/e8/e816a0fcde823bc6f6e88dff0a02c1877275cbed75757c1eb366fb224629127e.svg)

Now, the solution to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by $\mathbf{x}= A^{-1}\mathbf{b}.$ So, we compute $A^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1*: Find the determinant of $A.$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(1)-3(-2)+(-8) \\  & =1+6-8 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2*: Compute the matrix of minors.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & -7 \\ -1 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3*:  Find the matrix of cofactors.

![](images/be/beb80ea3185fc723c294313b63274554ec8af3531ed5643173a6127c59a21bb3.svg)

*Step 4*: Transpose the matrix of cofactors.

![](images/e6/e6fac5dd0a9918a03ce7c14e9cd05a06c6d11e95346f261ec75d6ebea09de1d6.svg)

*Step 5*: Apply the inverse matrix formula.

![](images/72/72b9d627d372d7a64a271b555b0d4cbb89b2bf9d602cdec64b1d8987a5e21521.svg)

Finally, we can calculate the solution as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10 \\ -33\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=3,$ $y=10,$ $z=-33.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186092187 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-0c58ffa5-e4d4-5bf5-8b35-8a71f48534ba"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-e321af2f-d67a-5dc4-a077-c6060845ea99" :question/id #uuid "e321af2f-d67a-5dc4-a077-c6060845ea99" :question/math-academy-id "q-78553" :question/problem "Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x+2y+z=3 \\ x-2y+z=1 \\ 2x-y+2z=5\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=-1,y=1,z=4.$

Finally, $x+y+z=-1+1+4=4.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-c0e50419-c826-5a89-9337-910bb9a469c2"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-c0e50419-c826-5a89-9337-910bb9a469c2" :answer-field/id #uuid "c0e50419-c826-5a89-9337-910bb9a469c2" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-ed96fe73-34bc-5554-8fe0-b110d7f3f6b3" :answer-field/choices ["answer-b90c4ae0-c1ef-52b6-b3de-1cbcb9e94c5e" "answer-f3dc6b18-74c4-595b-92c7-e48fa955a38e" "answer-d60be700-46fb-5903-a3f8-cfb1794eaf06" "answer-ed96fe73-34bc-5554-8fe0-b110d7f3f6b3" "answer-4fc306a8-65be-5769-9f23-972df29a47cd"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b90c4ae0-c1ef-52b6-b3de-1cbcb9e94c5e" :answer/id #uuid "b90c4ae0-c1ef-52b6-b3de-1cbcb9e94c5e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f3dc6b18-74c4-595b-92c7-e48fa955a38e" :answer/id #uuid "f3dc6b18-74c4-595b-92c7-e48fa955a38e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d60be700-46fb-5903-a3f8-cfb1794eaf06" :answer/id #uuid "d60be700-46fb-5903-a3f8-cfb1794eaf06" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-\frac{1}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ed96fe73-34bc-5554-8fe0-b110d7f3f6b3" :answer/id #uuid "ed96fe73-34bc-5554-8fe0-b110d7f3f6b3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4fc306a8-65be-5769-9f23-972df29a47cd" :answer/id #uuid "4fc306a8-65be-5769-9f23-972df29a47cd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-0807a9e2-ba3b-5d6e-8562-a580bc61f62a" :question/id #uuid "0807a9e2-ba3b-5d6e-8562-a580bc61f62a" :question/math-academy-id "q-104515" :question/problem "Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z=-1 \\ 3x-z=5+3y \\ 3z-2y=6-x\end{aligned}
$$

Find  $x+y+z.$" :question/worked-solution "First, let's rewrite the system in the correct order:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z=-1 \\ 3x-3y-z=5 \\ x-2y+3z=6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+(-2)|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-9-2)-(9+1)-2(-6+3) \\  & =-22-10+6 \\  & =-26.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-11 & 10 & -3 \\ -1 & 8 & -5 \\ -7 & 4 & -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-11 & -10 & -3 \\ 1 & 8 & 5 \\ -7 & -4 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-11 & 1 & -7 \\ -10 & 8 & -4 \\ -3 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}-11 & 1 & -7 \\ -10 & 8 & -4 \\ -3 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}-11 & 1 & -7 \\ -10 & 8 & -4 \\ -3 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}-26 \\ 26 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x+y+z=1-1+1=1.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d554649a-905d-57c6-af27-cc40c4c45a3a"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d554649a-905d-57c6-af27-cc40c4c45a3a" :answer-field/id #uuid "d554649a-905d-57c6-af27-cc40c4c45a3a" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-28126022-8f20-5f62-8417-0685db76f23b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3b9511ec-b4f9-5c7b-b596-beebd0bcb054" "answer-274c794a-3cbb-5dc2-bbb2-1f1131f70f1e" "answer-28126022-8f20-5f62-8417-0685db76f23b" "answer-0597b830-4974-5289-8d3c-e5ddb2d894f7" "answer-039d5f33-dfa0-51c2-93be-2b7000137d8a"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3b9511ec-b4f9-5c7b-b596-beebd0bcb054" :answer/id #uuid "3b9511ec-b4f9-5c7b-b596-beebd0bcb054" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-274c794a-3cbb-5dc2-bbb2-1f1131f70f1e" :answer/id #uuid "274c794a-3cbb-5dc2-bbb2-1f1131f70f1e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-28126022-8f20-5f62-8417-0685db76f23b" :answer/id #uuid "28126022-8f20-5f62-8417-0685db76f23b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0597b830-4974-5289-8d3c-e5ddb2d894f7" :answer/id #uuid "0597b830-4974-5289-8d3c-e5ddb2d894f7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-039d5f33-dfa0-51c2-93be-2b7000137d8a" :answer/id #uuid "039d5f33-dfa0-51c2-93be-2b7000137d8a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186237810 :question/problem "Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y-2z=-2 \\ -3y+z=-2 \\ 3x-7y+3z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}.$ Given that $\mathbf x = \langle x,y,z\rangle$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*
![](images/ad/add80202102548e61880979bc0379e0bc65f9ef7fa37173f9035410661e2b75e.png)" :question/worked-solution "First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & -7 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by $\mathbf{x}= A^{-1}\mathbf{b}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=3, y=0, z=-2.$

Finally, $x+y+z=3+0+(-2)=1.$"} {:db/id 17592186050825} {:db/id 17592186092817 :question/id #uuid "53eea4a9-49d1-52f4-a825-f27d06f9350d" :question/math-academy-id "q-78548"} {:db/id 17592186092818 $$

$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we organize the system so that the variables are in the correct order and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+3y+z=0 \\ 0x+4y+z=7 \\ 2x-y+0z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

![](images/97/97d3c148b792d9db50bc81b8c12f1574f284746cb37b12d99a8881853bf5ea13.png)

Now, the solution to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by $\mathbf{x}= A^{-1}\mathbf{b}.$ So, we compute $A^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1*: Find the determinant of $A.$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(1)-3(-2)+(-8) \\  & =1+6-8 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2*: Compute the matrix of minors.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & -7 \\ -1 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3*:  Find the matrix of cofactors.

![](images/e9/e93ae11a2b2d1538c4ad97bba6d92e8e17fe14c8778898365ffeda9c5d1bacee.png)

*Step 4*: Transpose the matrix of cofactors.

![](images/c2/c2492650916d7a880ea52322edb41b8127b4c31bcff0620cec3cf4e37fa7928f.png)

*Step 5*: Apply the inverse matrix formula.

![](images/dd/dd70742ae3c6613f78305edc718b10568269b49be611643059a1e6121828f404.png)

Finally, we can calculate the solution as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10 \\ -33\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=3,$ $y=10,$ $z=-33.$"} {:db/id 17592186049043} {:db/id 17592186092709 :question/id #uuid "be9d95c2-a710-5571-987b-8cd6ddd0d0ab" :question/math-academy-id "q-42449"} {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "2997dd93-b478-5bad-935c-182c80540138" :question/math-academy-id "q-10091" :question/problem "Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+2z=0 \\ x+2y+3z=2 \\ 3x+y+z=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-1(1-9)+2(1-6) \\  & =+8-10 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 & -5 \\ -1 & -6 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 8 & -5 \\ 1 & -6 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -1 \\ 8 & -6 & 2 \\ -5 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -1 \\ 8 & -6 & 2 \\ -5 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -8 & 6 & -2 \\ 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
